migrate/migrate.up.cite:
(1) The task body.  activerecord-8.0.5.1 lib/active_record/railties/databases.rake:89-92 is now `task migrate: :load_config do ActiveRecord::Tasks::DatabaseTasks.migrate_all; db_namespace["_dump"].invoke end`.  activerecord-7.2.3.2's copy of that file, at the same line 89, opens the identical task and calls `ActiveRecord::Tasks::DatabaseTasks.migrate` directly (:89-107); the word `migrate_all` does not occur anywhere in 7.2.3.2 lib/active_record/tasks/database_tasks.rb (grep count 0).
(2) What `migrate_all` adds.  activerecord-8.0.5.1 lib/active_record/tasks/database_tasks.rb:243-260: `db_configs.each { |db_config| initialize_database(db_config) }`, then `DatabaseTasks.migrate(skip_initialize: true)`.  The initialisation is :660-678: `database_already_initialized = migration_connection_pool.schema_migration.table_exists?`, rescuing `ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError` by creating the database and retrying, and then `unless database_already_initialized` -- `schema_dump_path = schema_dump_path(db_config); if schema_dump_path && File.exist?(schema_dump_path); load_schema(db_config); end`.  `initialize_database` does not exist in activerecord-7.2.3.2 (grep count 0 in the same file), and 7.2.3.2's `migrate` at :256 takes `(version = nil)` with no `skip_initialize:` keyword -- the whole branch is new.
(3) The release note.  activerecord-8.0.5.1 CHANGELOG.md:621: "When running `db:migrate` on a fresh database, load the databases schemas before running migrations."  *Andrew Novoselac*, *Marek Kasztelnik*.
(4) Measured on the golden, and on the tree this step is handed.  The step 10 recording this fragment copies its `obs` from: /tmp/f10g/logs/verifier/observed.json, world `migrate`, case `migrate/migrate.up` -- `exit_ok` true, `aborted` false, `stdout.events` empty -- taken in the same run whose `migrate.status_after` reads 44 rows and whose `migrate.version_after` reads 20160119120000.  The same tree with `db/schema.rb` moved aside runs all 44 migrations and prints 88 `==` banners, which is how the two branches were told apart rather than assumed.
migrate/migrate.up.why:
`prepare_migrate` tears the database down -- `db:drop`, `db:create` -- and then runs `db:migrate` against a database with no `schema_migrations` table, which is the one place in this task where the 44 migration files under db/migrate/ are all run in order.  From 8.0 that is no longer what the task does.  `db:migrate` now initialises an uninitialised database from `db/schema.rb` *before* it looks for pending migrations, so the dump is loaded, every version it names is inserted into `schema_migrations`, and the migration pass that follows finds nothing to do: the recorded event stream goes from 142 events -- 44 `migrating` banners and the operations under them -- to none at all.  Measured on the golden: build/gold/10, `db:drop db:create db:migrate` prints 2 lines and runs 0 migrations with the dump in place and 286 lines and all 44 with it moved aside.
Nothing else in the world moves, and that is the shape of the change rather than an accident of what was recorded.  `migrate.status_after` still lists 44 rows and all of them still read `up`, `migrate.version_after` still reports 20160119120000, and the IVR the world then drives over that database answers exactly as it did -- because `load_schema` builds the same seven tables and records the same versions.  What changed is which of the two constructions `db:migrate` performs, and the only reading that can see the difference is the one that watches it work.  `migrate.up_again`, the adversarial second `db:migrate` over an already-migrated schema, was silent before and is silent now; `migrate.down_one` and `migrate.up_one` still print their three events each, because `db:migrate:down` and `db:migrate:up` do not go through `migrate_all` and never had this behaviour.
As a must-flip this is worth more than the event stream it replaces.  A tree still on 7.2 cannot produce it: on 7.2 the 44 banners are printed, and a tree that has reached 8.0 cannot suppress them selectively either, because the branch is taken on `schema_migration.table_exists?` and not on anything the application configures.  Silence here together with 44 `up` rows in `migrate.status_after` is a fact about the framework version and about nothing else.
The independent construction this world used to provide is not lost, it has moved to where it can still be had: `test.sh` now removes `db/schema.rb` before the `dbmigrate` run that feeds `pkdrift`, so the comparison between the dump-built database and the migration-built one is still between two databases built two different ways, on 8.0 as on every rung before it.
